title: Hˢ Ascent Path and Controlled Growth Trajectory
prepared_from: Conversation with Peter about staged repo depth, controlled revision, learning path, governance, compositional analysis, and future trajectory
primary_goal: Help Peter develop a coherent staged-ascent architecture for the Hˢ repository, so user learning, engine capabilities, documentation depth, governance, and project revision all advance together in controlled stages.

Overloading first-time users with the full conceptual stack
Making the project feel obscure, ominous, or inaccessible

important_user_preferences: Peter likes staged depth in the repo
Peter wants positive upward language rather than descent or dungeon imagery
Peter sees governance and compositional analysis as interwoven because they spawned from the same roots

conversation_summary.major_strategic_conclusion: The project should not separate governance from compositional analysis. Instead, it should stage them together through an ascent model where users begin with practical use and climb toward method, evidence, provenance, AI assistance, integration, and canon stewardship only when their work requires it.

core_thesis.short_form: Hˢ should be staged for ascent.
core_thesis.long_form: The repository should guide users from ground-level recognition of compositional data to progressively higher capabilities: running an analysis, interpreting results, understanding simplex movement, comparing evidence, governing reproducibility, using AI safely, extending domains, integrating into larger systems, and contributing to canon.
core_thesis.why_it_matters: The repo has grown through continuous discovery. Without staged ascent, every refinement ripples through README, glossary, appendix, conference framing, AI refresh, governance protocol, and user docs. The ascent model allows discovery to continue while revision is promoted through deliberate gates.

project_identity.short_description: Hˢ is a compositional analysis and governance project that makes finite-system change operational, reproducible, and auditable.
project_identity.science_value: It provides reproducible compositional instrumentation for systems where internal proportions matter more than totals.
project_identity.industry_value: It turns mix change into a measurable and auditable event across finite-share systems such as energy portfolios, budgets, supplier allocations, product mix, defect categories, materials fractions, and case mix.
project_identity.governance_value: It gives users, reviewers, and AI assistants controlled gates for authority, provenance, reproducibility, claim strength, and revision.
project_identity.unifying_root: Finite constrained change requires accountable attribution.

ascent_path.recommended_subtitle: From First Composition to Governed Instrument
ascent_path.opening_text: Hˢ is staged for ascent. Begin at the ground layer: recognize a composition and run one dataset. Ascend only when your question requires more power: interpretation, geometry, reference comparison, provenance, AI assistance, integration, or canon revision. Each ascent level gives three things: a user ability, an engine capability, and a documentation depth. You do not need the summit to use the instrument. You climb when the work asks for it.

levels.name: Ground
levels.user_ability: The user can identify whether their dataset is compositional.
levels.documentation_depth: A short page explaining rows, carriers, labels, closure, percentages, fractions, shares, and finite wholes.
levels.gate: The user can distinguish carriers from labels and confirm that the data describes parts of a whole.
levels.claim_discipline: No advanced claims. Only determine whether the data belongs in the instrument.

levels.name: First Ascent
levels.user_ability: The user can get a valid first result from a dataset.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: CCTT phases for diagnosing data, selecting or generating an adapter, and running the engine.
levels.gate: Carrier mapping is confirmed by the user before analysis is accepted.
levels.claim_discipline: The result is a first valid compositional read, not a broad scientific claim.

levels.name: Report Reading
levels.user_ability: The user can interpret the basic report without understanding the full method stack.
levels.documentation_depth: A guide titled something like Reading a Stage 1 Report.
levels.gate: The user can summarize what changed without inventing claims beyond the report.
levels.claim_discipline: Interpretation must remain inside what the engine output supports.

levels.name: Simplex Movement
levels.user_ability: The user understands why raw differences are not enough for closed compositions.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Stage 2 and Stage 3 outputs when the data supports temporal or structural interpretation.
levels.documentation_depth: Closure, Aitchison geometry, carrier redistribution, trajectory shape, and why gains imply losses elsewhere.
levels.gate: The user can distinguish raw magnitude change from compositional redistribution.
levels.claim_discipline: Geometry enters only when needed; it should not burden first-time users.

levels.name: Evidence Comparison
levels.user_ability: The user can compare their result to reference examples, known patterns, prior runs, or named findings.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Reference comparisons, fingerprints, corpus matching, or replay against known examples.
levels.documentation_depth: Experiments journal, reference corpus guide, worked examples, and named findings.
levels.gate: The user can classify the result as known, new, similar, unstable, or out of scope.
levels.claim_discipline: Comparison does not automatically promote a result to canon.

levels.name: Governed Result
levels.user_ability: The user can explain what was run, on what data, with what adapter, under what version, and with what reproducibility evidence.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Schema validation, source hash, rerun hash, output hash, journal, and verification checks.
levels.documentation_depth: Operations Protocol, CCTT Runbook, hash-manifest rules, and reproducibility notes.
levels.gate: The user can prove or document reproducibility and provenance.
levels.claim_discipline: A governed result is stronger than a run result because it has receipts.

levels.name: AI-Assisted Operation
levels.user_ability: The user can use an AI assistant while preserving human authority.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Same protocol, same gates, same hashes; AI may execute but not govern.
levels.documentation_depth: AI-assisted CCTT guide, AI refresh rules, grounding tests, and human-confirmation doctrine.
levels.gate: The user can identify which decisions must not be outsourced to the AI.
levels.claim_discipline: AI fluency is not authority. The AI must pass grounding and operate inside the same gates.

levels.name: Domain Extension
levels.theme: Bring a new domain into the instrument
levels.user_ability: The user can adapt Hˢ to a new compositional domain.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Adapter generation, corpus comparison, staged reporting, and result packaging.
levels.documentation_depth: Adapter guide, domain-example guide, promotion packet template, and claims register.
levels.gate: The user decides whether the result remains a one-off example or deserves promotion into references, examples, or public claims.
levels.claim_discipline: New domain use does not automatically become a general method claim.

levels.name: System Integration
levels.user_ability: The user can embed Hˢ as a component in a larger workflow, research process, governance system, or industrial monitor.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Controller, events, audit trail, monitoring outputs, and governed operation.
levels.documentation_depth: Architecture overview, platform guide, applications guide, and integration patterns.
levels.gate: The user can define whether Hˢ is acting as monitor, classifier, early-warning instrument, audit layer, governance layer, or analysis engine.
levels.claim_discipline: Integration should preserve the instrument boundary and not blur evidence, governance, and automation.

levels.name: Canon Stewardship
levels.user_ability: The user can propose changes without destabilizing the project.
levels.engine_capability_exposed: Regression checks, reference corpus, authority stack, reproducibility tests, and canon-update workflow.
levels.documentation_depth: Claims Register, Glossary Canon, Promotion Log, Operations Protocol, and Root Change Note template.
levels.gate: The contribution is classified as leaf, branch, trunk, or root before it alters canonical files.
levels.claim_discipline: Canon changes require promotion, not ripple.

controlled_growth_model.central_rule: Discovery may be simultaneous. Revision must be staged.

leaf.meaning: Examples, slides, notes, named findings, dated refreshes, discussion drafts, appendix expansions.
leaf.change_policy: May grow freely. Does not automatically alter public canon.

branch.meaning: Applications, venue-specific work, conference materials, industry examples, domain adapters, case studies.
branch.change_policy: May consolidate from leaves. Should not casually rewrite trunk.

trunk.meaning: Canonical instruments and doctrines such as Hˢ identity, CNT and CNQ distinction, CCTT workflow, operations protocol, claim-strength rules, canonical glossary, AI refresh authority stack.
trunk.change_policy: Requires deliberate promotion and downstream review.

root.meaning: Foundational concepts generating the project, such as finite systems, closure, compositional change, carrier-level attribution, governance as controlled transformation, human authority over AI assistance, and reproducibility.
root.change_policy: Changes rarely and requires doctrine review.

phase_1.name: Stabilize the metaphor
phase_1.goal: Adopt ascent language across the repo without restructuring everything at once.
actions: Replace descent or depth-only phrasing with ascent phrasing where user-facing
Introduce the phrase Start at the ground. Ascend as needed.
Keep depth as structure but use ascent as movement
phase_1.risk_to_avoid: Cosmetic renaming without changing user navigation

phase_2.name: Create the Ascent Path front door
phase_2.goal: Give users a clear staged capability ladder.
actions: Create docs/HS_ASCENT_PATH.md
Preserve the older learning path as historical or legacy if needed
Add a short README pointer for new users, dataset users, reviewers, AI users, and contributors
phase_2.risk_to_avoid: Making the new path too long or too theoretical

phase_3.name: Align engine stages with documentation stages
phase_3.goal: Make the engine's progressive outputs correspond to user learning levels.
actions: Map Stage 1 output to Ascent 2
Map temporal and structural outputs to Ascent 3
Map reference comparison to Ascent 4
Map hashes and self-verification to Ascent 5
Map AI-assisted operation to Ascent 6
phase_3.risk_to_avoid: Showing deeper outputs before the user has the interpretive ability to read them

phase_4.name: Install controlled revision flow
phase_4.goal: Prevent every discovery from rippling through all documents immediately.
actions: Create a promotion packet template
Create or formalize a claims register
Create a promotion log
Classify changes as leaf, branch, trunk, or root
phase_4.risk_to_avoid: Letting promotion bureaucracy slow discovery itself

phase_5.name: Prepare the CoDaWork bridge
phase_5.goal: Use the ascent architecture to keep the conference front door clean.
actions: Keep CoDaWork talk at the method and evidence layers
Avoid overloading the talk with full governance or AI-refresh internals
Use named findings, caveats, and defeat paths as the evidence layer
Let deeper governance appear only if asked
phase_5.risk_to_avoid: Trying to present the entire repo arc in a 15-minute talk

phase_6.name: Post-conference adoption layer
phase_6.goal: Make the repo useful for future scientific and industry users.
actions: Provide a dataset-user path
Provide a reviewer path
Provide an industry-monitor path
Provide an AI-assisted path
Provide a contributor or canon-stewardship path
phase_6.risk_to_avoid: Assuming all future users are CoDa specialists

conference_context.recommended_posture: Enter through the accepted abstract and standard CoDa framing, not through the entire Hˢ mythology.
conference_context.talk_strategy: Present the energy-mix drift result, name the empirical findings, visibly caveat null-model limits, and invite defeat paths from the CoDa audience.
what_to_avoid: Trying to prove the whole framework
Presenting governance as the lead claim
Overloading a 15-minute talk with repo architecture
conference_context.bridge_sentence: The conference talk is an ascent waypoint, not the summit.

science: A way to reproduce and challenge proportional-change claims
future_user_value.shared_value: Bring a compositional dataset. Confirm the carrier mapping. Run the instrument. Keep the receipts.

principles_to_preserve: The user should not be shown more math than their current action requires.
The engine should not expose deeper interpretation until the data supports it.
Documentation should not force canon, history, and governance into the first encounter.
AI assistants should not skip the ascent just because they can read fast.
Revisions should promote upward only through gates.
Historical files explain how the project got here. Canon files say where the project is now.
Discovery grows outward. Canon changes inward. Publication flows downward. History flows backward.
Not all discoveries are claims. Not all claims are public. Not all public claims are root doctrine.
